title: Copying Files: `docker cp` 📁
description: Move files between your host machine and containers with ease.

slides.title: The Data Bridge 🌉
slides.content:
# `docker cp`

Sometimes you need to get a file **into** a container (config files, certificates) or **out of** it (logs, generated data) without setting up volumes.

```bash
docker cp [OPTIONS] SRC_PATH DEST_PATH
```

One of the paths must be a container reference (e.g., `my-container:/path`).

- **Host to container:** `docker cp ./config.txt my-container:/app/config.txt`
- **Container to host:** `docker cp my-container:/var/log/app.log ./app.log`

slides.title: Copy Examples 📤📥
slides.content: Let’s copy a file into and out of a container:
slides.codeSnippet:
# Create a dummy file on host
echo "Hello Docker" > greet.txt

# Start a container
docker run -d --name storage alpine sleep 600

# Copy file into container
docker cp greet.txt storage:/tmp/greet.txt

# Verify inside container
docker exec storage cat /tmp/greet.txt

# Copy file out of container (simulate log export)
docker exec storage sh -c 'echo log entry > /var/log/app.log'
docker cp storage:/var/log/app.log ./app.log

# Cleanup
docker rm -f storage

quizData.question: Which command copies a local file `data.csv` into a container named `db` at `/opt/data.csv`?
quizData.explanation: The syntax is `SOURCE DEST`. To copy from host to container, the host path comes first.

slides.title: cp Only Works with Containers 🚫
slides.content:
## Not for Images

`docker cp` works on **containers** (running or stopped). You cannot copy files to/from an image directly. If you need that, use Dockerfile `COPY` or `ADD`.

slides.title: Permissions & Ownership 👮
slides.content:
# Gotchas

- The copied file inherits the user and group of the process that runs `docker cp` on the host side (unless the destination path already exists with different ownership).
- Inside the container, files are owned by the user executing the `cp` command (host’s `docker` client).
- For containers, you can use `--archive` (`-a`) to preserve ownership and timestamps (only from container to host, not both ways).

```bash
docker cp -a my-container:/etc/hosts ./
```
